name: Valle de la Luna: the Duna Mayor walk
region: Valle de la Luna, Cordillera de la Sal, Atacama
why: A sand ridge above the salt-crusted Cordillera de la Sal: from the top of the great dune the valley's eroded ridges run to Licancabur and the Andes.
book: Ticket online (valledelaluna.com, run by the Asociación Indígena Valle de la Luna with CONAF; CLP 10,800 general). You cannot enter on foot: come by car, tour or bicycle (bikes enter 08:00/09:00-11:00). Tres Marías and the salt caves are further stops by vehicle.
water: None in the valley and no shop, only toilets at the entrance: carry 1.5 litres even for this short walk.
dangers: Strong sun, no shade and dry air at 2,500 m: hat and sunscreen.
Stay on the marked path: the ridge edges are soft sand and crumbling salt, and the side paths are closed.
The reserve closes on red-alert heat days and after earthquakes: check the notice on the site before you go.
turnaround: Walk back when the rangers announce closing time: vehicles must leave by 17:30 (winter) and the valley shuts after it.

points.name: Duna Mayor car park
points.note: The stop on the valley road where the marked path leaves for the dune; tours and bikes stop here.

points.name: Duna Mayor viewpoint
points.note: The first lookout on the dune crest, over the great sand slope and the salt ridges of the Cordillera de la Sal.

points.name: Duna Mayor ridge end
points.note: Where the ridge path ends, with the Valle de la Luna and the Andean volcanoes in one view. Back the same way.
